findings.excerpt: For C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²), a finite-dimensional graded real module M=M^0⊕M^1 determines the ABS symbol triple (π^*M^0,π^*M^1,c(v)) on the disk/sphere pair of ℝ^n: over a nonzero vector v, Clifford multiplication c(v) is an isomorphism because c(v)^2=−‖v‖²I. Its relative KO class is the candidate symbol. The separate theorem proves that the symbol vanishes on restrictions from C_(n+1), descends to A_n, and is an isomorphism.
findings.symptom: The screenshot renders the formula notation as ordinary ASCII text (including C_n, M^0, π^*, c(v), and C_(n+1)) rather than typeset mathematics throughout the definition.
findings.suggested_repair: Wrap the mathematical expressions in supported math delimiters and use renderer-compatible subscripts, superscripts, and operators.

findings.excerpt: For n≥0 put C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²). Let M_n be the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional real Z/2-graded left C_n-modules and let r_n:M_{n+1}→M_n be restriction along the standard inclusion of the first n Clifford generators. Define A_n=coker(r_n). For n=0 the grading is retained, so M_0≅Z⊕Z from even and odd dimensions; no parity type is identified with a volume-element eigenspace.
findings.symptom: The screenshot shows the notation in the entire definition as plain ASCII (for example C_n, r_n, M_{n+1}, and A_n=coker(r_n)) rather than typeset mathematics.
findings.suggested_repair: Set the mathematical expressions in supported math delimiters with proper subscripts, superscripts, and operator formatting.

findings.excerpt: Assume AC. Let W be the CW wedge of any set of spheres of dimensions at least c≥2. For 1≤i≤2c−2, π_i(W)⊗Q and H_i(W;Q) are the direct sum of Q indexed by spheres of dimension i, and actual Hurewicz identifies their orientation generators.
findings.symptom: The screenshot displays the statement’s mathematical notation as plain text (e.g. π_i(W)⊗Q, H_i(W;Q), and the range 1≤i≤2c−2), without mathematical typesetting.
findings.suggested_repair: Wrap the mathematical notation in supported math delimiters and render the range and groups as typeset formulas.

findings.excerpt: Assume AC. For f_r:T_r→P_r, f_{r*}:H_i(T_r;Z)→H_i(P_r;Z) is an isomorphism for i<2r−1 and a surjection for i=2r−1. No endpoint injectivity is asserted.
findings.symptom: The screenshot renders the statement formulas as unstyled literal text, including f_r, f_{r*}, H_i, and the endpoint range, rather than typeset mathematics.
findings.suggested_repair: Put the mathematical expressions in supported math delimiters with proper subscripts and superscripts.

findings.excerpt: Assume AC. For every r≥0 and every i≥0, H_i(MO(r);Z) and H_i(MSO(r);Z) are finitely generated. For positive rank the locally constructed homological Thom comparison is H_i(D(γ_r),S(γ_r);Z)=H_{i−r}(BO(r);O_Z(γ_r)), and likewise for γ_r⁺ with the constant orientation system. The disk/sphere quotient identifies these groups with reduced Thom homology. At rank zero the based quotient is B₊; BO(0)=BSO(0)=* gives S⁰ and is handled separately.
findings.symptom: The screenshot shows the statement’s formula-heavy notation as ordinary unformatted characters, including H_i, MO(r), MSO(r), γ_r, and O_Z(γ_r).
findings.suggested_repair: Wrap mathematical notation in supported math delimiters and use typeset subscripts, superscripts, and symbols.
